paragraphs: Mentioned in Berakhot, chapter 1, halakhah 1, at the additional printed page locator 4b. But Yoma, chapter 3, halakhah 1, and Bereshit Rabbah 50:10 read R' Chanina.
A nun and a yod became a tsadi.[^1][^2][^3]

notes.text: פ״נ-י is contextually 50:10 without independently verified modern correspondence, rather than an unexplained yod or a source repair.

ה״א-ד: is interpreted as halakhah 1 plus additional historical page 4b, not halakhot 1–4. The unusual colon after ביומא is preserved in the source, read with the next-line 3h 1; corpus remains unstated, without fresh print check.

Hyman’s nun+yod→tsadi explanation is preserved literally in the body, with the implied reading-together mechanism only explanatory. It is not a new image review or admitted correction history. Chatzna/Chanina remain distinct and both titles R'.
